newsitem.title: FRANCE: Libya's Gaddafi hails Clinton. Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi hails Clinton. Chirac.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi has good words for the leaders of two countries confronting him over airliner bombings, calling U.S. President Bill Clinton "a good man", and French President Jacques Chirac courageous.

Gaddafi told the French newspaper Le Figaro in an interview published on Monday that Clinton, a democrat, had been hampered by the Republicans' legacy in his first term but would have a free hand in the second term he has just won.
"Bill Clinton is a good man...(he) inherited problems created by the Republicans," Gaddafi said.
Describing Clinton's first four-year term as a time when rivers of blood ran in Lebanon, Iraq, Bosnia, Somalia and Liberia, he said: "It all happened despite Clinton's good intentions.
"He is now free of the hypocrisy needed to be re-elected, he escapes the Zionist lobby's electoral pressure...The world will at last discover Bill Clinton's true personality," he said.
Gaddafi said there was no progress in his dispute with Washington and London over the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland in which 270 people died.
"We accuse the U.S. and British authorities of multiplying obstacles because they know the accused Libyans are innocent," he said.
But he said that, under Chirac, Libya could solve the dispute over the 1989 mid-air bombing of a French UTA airliner in which 170 died.

"With Jacques Chirac, a courageous man who unlike (the late Socialist French president Francois) Mitterrand does not submit to American diktats I think we are on the way to a settlement," Gaddafi said.

The Security Council in 1992 imposed an arms and air embargo on Libya to force it to hand over for trial two of its citizens suspected in the Lockerbie bombing and cooperate with the French probe. Gaddafi says the trial would only be acceptable in a third country.
French anti-terrorism investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere recently visited Libya and added two Libyan suspects to the four he wants handed over for trial.
In other part of the interview, Gaddafi said there was an international conspiracy to lock up Jews in Israel, a country he described as their grave.
"I urge them to go home. Home is everywhere: Libya, Africa, Russia, even Alaska," he said.
Gaddafi said hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was "no liar".
"He is a Zionist who speaks clear and loud. He says squarely: 'I want to eliminate the Arabs and achieve Israeli interests'." Gaddafi said.
He described Islamic fundamentalists as reactionary and puzzled by the rapid progress of sciences. "They ban what thay cannot understand," he said.

A man from the desert, Gaddafi called cities the cemetery of civilisation and said they had never produced any prophet. "The city is an atomic bomb created by man and he cannot live there. Men must get rid of cities," he said.
